newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House panel said to back new rail agency.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House panel said to back new rail agency.

text.p: An advisory group formed by the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee will recommend on Monday the creation of a new federal agency to own or manage track used by passenger trains, the Washington Post reported.
Under the group's proposal, Amtrak, the troubled passenger train system, and other rail operators would compete for contractors to run the trains, the newspaper reported in its Monday editions.
The new agency, called Amrail by the advisory panel, would own only the Washington-Boston corridor and a few shorter stretches of track in New York, Pennsylvania and Michigan.

The Working Group on Intercity Passenger Rail was formed by committee chairman Bud Schuster, a Pennsylvania Republican, out of frustration with Congress's failure to agree on Amtrak's future. It has no legislative powers.
The group's plan is almost identical to one being implemented in Britain, the Post said, noting that most U.S. track was owned by private freight railroads.
On routes owned freight railroads, Amrail would pay for necessary improvements to expand passenger service while leaving room for burgeoning rail freight service.
The advisory panel's report said Amtrak appeared to be only six to 12 months from possible bankruptcy and has lost more than $700 million in each of the last nine years.

Amtrak Chairman Thomas Downs told Congress in April that additional money was needed to keep the rail service in business. He said Amtrak was already borrowing money to meet its payroll and needed several billion dollars in the coming years to complete a modernization effort that includes buying 18 high speed trains for its busy East Coast corridor.

Senate Finance Committee Chairman William Roth, a Delaware Republican, last week proposed funding for Amtrak at a cost of $2.3 billion over five years, paid for with a half-cent of a 4.3-cents-per-gallon gasoline tax.
